Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "Flintec UK Ltd"
- Document: "Flintec"

Is this the same entity? The document says just "Flintec" while the register says "Flintec UK Ltd". This is truncation — the document's extraction only captured "Flintec". Is that spelling drift/legal-suffix drift (same-entity), or a different entity?

The rules:
- spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity
- Extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise) = document-noise with best_value from the register
- Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's)

"Flintec" vs "Flintec UK Ltd" — this looks like truncation during extraction. The certificate's own comment header even says applicant: Flintec UK Ltd (in the embedded metadata comments: `<!-- applicant: Flintec UK Ltd -->`). Wait, look at the document context:

"<!-- cert_id: 4620 --> <!-- num: R60/2000-A-GB1-18.01 --> <!-- applicant: Flintec UK Ltd --> ..."

So the document context itself (extraction comments) says "Flintec UK Ltd". But the conflict statement says document: "Flintec". Hmm — perhaps the visible table text says "Flintec" (the table is truncated: "United Kingdom of Great Br..." — cut off). So the document surface value extracted from the visible text is "Flintec".

The choice: same-entity vs document-noise. "Flintec" is a truncation of "Flintec UK Ltd" — likely an extraction artifact (truncated text from PDF, as the table text itself is cut off at "United Kingdom of Great Br"). But per rules, truncation could be considered... The rules give three relevant categories:
1. same-entity: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences
2. document-noise: extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into name, OCR noise) — best_value from register
3. different-entity: genuinely different names — best_value from document

"Flintec" vs "Flintec UK Ltd" — this is a truncation, not really "spelling drift" or "legal-suffix drift". Legal-suffix drift would be like "Flintec UK Ltd" vs "Flintec UK Limited" or "Flintec UK" vs "Flintec UK Ltd". Here the document just says "Flintec" — the company family name without the UK/Ltd. It's arguably truncation, which is an extraction artifact (the table is visibly truncated). But "obvious OCR noise" examples given are address fragments glued in, OCR noise. A truncation of the name is arguably an extraction artifact too.

However, "same-entity" with best value — which best value? The rules say for same-entity, examples like "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." For applicant same-entity, presumably best value would be the more complete one — the register's "Flintec UK Ltd" (or the document's?). Actually for same-entity on names, typically the more complete/canonical form. The register is canonical.

Hmm, but wait — "Flintec" alone could refer to Flintec AB (Sweden) or Flintec UK Ltd, etc. But within this certificate context (GB1 issuer, NMO UK, "United Kingdom of Great Br..."), the applicant is clearly Flintec UK Ltd. So same-entity.

Verdict choice: I'd say "same-entity" — the document value is a truncated form of the same company name; best_value = "Flintec UK Ltd" (register's canonical form, more complete). Alternatively "document-noise" because truncation is an extraction artifact. The rules define document-noise as "Extraction artifacts (address fragments glued into a name, obvious OCR noise) = document-noise with best_value from the register." Truncation of a name could be considered an extraction artifact. But the distinction between same-entity and document-noise: same-entity is about the value being a variant of the same name; document-noise is about the value being corrupted by unrelated content. "Flintec" is a prefix of "Flintec UK Ltd" — it's a partial extraction, not noise glued in. Hmm.

Given the visible table text is truncated ("United Kingdom of Great Br"), the "Flintec" value likely came from a truncated PDF text extraction. That leans toward document-noise (extraction artifact) with best_value from register = "Flintec UK Ltd".

But the simplest reading per rules: "Flintec" vs "Flintec UK Ltd" is essentially name truncation / suffix drop = same entity. The verdict same-entity with best_value "Flintec UK Ltd" seems right. Actually, either verdict could justify best_value = register value. The difference is in "why".

I think "same-entity" is the safer verdict: it's clearly the same company, just a shortened name. Document-noise is for artifacts like OCR junk, address fragments — "Flintec" is not noise, it's a valid short form (the company brand). So same-entity, best_value = "Flintec UK Ltd" (register canonical, more complete/precise).

One sentence why: The document value is a truncated/short form of the same company name; the register's "Flintec UK Ltd" is the fuller canonical entity name, corroborated by the certificate's own metadata comment.
